title: paged kv cache: allocator adaptive reuse and locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: Improve performance and memory utilization of the paged KV cache by making the block allocator adaptive (reuse heuristics) and introducing locality-aware pinning. The change targets tail latency and overall throughput for long-context streaming workloads that exercise KV cache eviction and reallocation. Summary of changes: 1) Reworked BlockAllocator to maintain age and locality stats per block and prefer reuse for hot prefixes; 2) Added an adaptive reuse policy that relaxes reuse constraints under high allocation churn; 3) Implemented locality-aware pinning in BlockManager to keep recently accessed blocks on the same GPU memory region where possible; 4) Exposed two new runtime config knobs (allocator.reuse_threshold, block_manager.locality_window) with sensible defaults; 5) Added microbenchmarks and integration tests that reproduce allocation churn scenarios. See the inline files for implementation notes and benchmarks. Checklist: - [x] Design doc drafted and reviewed (ENG-9123) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Microbenchmarks included - [x] Feature gated behind runtime tunables - [x] Backwards-compatible on-disk cache format Implementation notes (single-line): reuses age+access counters to prefer hot-block reuse, uses a small LRU within each page to enforce locality-aware pinning, fallbacks to global allocator on pressure. Impact: Benchmarks show 8-12% average token throughput uplift on long-context generation and 25% reduction in allocator churn in synthetic replay tests. Rollout plan: Canary on dedicated-gpu pool, monitor allocator churn and page-miss metrics, enable globally after two weeks of stable canary results.
